uncertainties_and_exclusions: Original microanalysis gives approximate Fe0.6In2S4 for one result and variable Fe0.6-1In1.2-2.4S4 for multiple grains; accepted formula is ideal species identity.
Nearly all observed indite grains were variably replaced by dzhalindite. Sampling and phase picking are not a guarantee of pure bulk feed.
Figure6 compares natural diffraction with earlier synthetic data; the 311 intensity mismatch is retained rather than silently equating all profiles.
Hahn/Klingler1950 FeIn2S4 synthesis at900C/12h is cited secondary evidence, not natural indite crystallization conditions.
Separate dzhalindite heating and hydroxide comparisons in Tables4-7 are not indite transformation experiments.
Table8 reuses Komarova/Novorosova1959 cassiterite chemistry. It is not a new independent indite extraction experiment.
Concentrated nitric-acid etching of polished sections and hot fuming sulfuric-acid dissolution of tiny separate grains differ in geometry/conditions; no quantitative recovery claim imported.
Printed original445-457 and Handbook agree; older445-458 bibliographic rendering is superseded for this original. Sixteen PDF pages include three inserted plates.
No microbial, metal-recovery or criticality assertion is made; omission is not proof that no such literature exists.
